newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka sells plantation stake at premium.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka sells plantation stake at premium.

text.p: Sri Lanka on Friday sold a controlling 51 percent stake in state-owned Maturata Plantations at a premium, brokers said.
They said the 51 percent equity stake, introduced at a minimum price of 30 rupees a share, was bought by the Employees Trust Fund, a state-managed gratuity fund, at 45.75 rupees per 10-rupee share.
The sale of Maturata is part of the government's privatisation process. Two more plantations will be privatised next week with the sale of 51 percent stakes in them.

An official of the Public Enterprise Reform Commission (PERC), the state arm which oversees privatisation, said earlier this week that 10.2 million shares, or 51 percent of Maturata's equity, would be sold on the stock exchange.

The official, who declined to be identified, told Reuters that the three pre-qualified bidders to take part in the sale were the Employees Trust Fund, Crop Management Services Ltd, a unit of Chemical Industries and Wayamba Plantations Lanka (Pvt) Ltd.

PERC said 51 percent or 10.2 million shares in Namunukula Plantations and Malwatte Plantations would also be sold on the stock exchange on June 2 and 4, respectively, at a minimum price of 30 rupees a share.
